questions.question: What was the first published poetry collection by Vinod Kumar Shukla?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lagbhag Jai Hind**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lagbhag Jai Hind** is the first poetry collection by renowned Indian poet and author **Vinod Kumar Shukla**.
 
• It was first published in the year **1971** and marks the beginning of Vinod Kumar Shukla's literary journey as a poet.
 
• The collection reflects Shukla's distinctive style of blending profound philosophical thoughts with simple and everyday language.
 
• Vinod Kumar Shukla is known for his unique and thought-provoking contributions to Hindi literature, with this poetry collection being a significant milestone in his career.
 
• His works often explore themes of human emotions, social realities, and philosophical insights, and "Lagbhag Jai Hind" is no exception.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinod Kumar Shukla's Literary Style:**

 
 
• Shukla is celebrated for his minimalist and evocative writing style.
 
• His works often blend realism with surrealism, creating a unique narrative voice in Hindi literature.
 
• He uses simple language to convey complex ideas, making his works accessible yet deeply philosophical.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Works by Vinod Kumar Shukla:**
 
 
• His novel **"Naukar Ki Kameez"** (The Servant's Shirt) gained critical acclaim and was adapted into a film by Mani Kaul.
 
• Another notable work, **"Deewar Mein Ek Khidki Rehti Thi"** (There Used to Be a Window in the Wall), reflects his mastery in storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Recognition and Awards:**
 
 
• Vinod Kumar Shukla has been awarded prestigious honors like the **Sahitya Akademi Award** for his contributions to Hindi literature.
 
• His works are celebrated for their originality and depth, establishing him as one of the key figures in modern Hindi literature.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Hindi Poetry:**
 
 
• Shukla's poetry often challenges traditional notions of poetic expression, focusing on the beauty of the mundane.
 
• His works have inspired a new generation of poets to embrace simplicity and innovation in their writing.

questions.question: According to the Law of Periods, the square of a planet's time period is proportional to:

options.text: The square of its distance from the sun
The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit
The square root of its orbital radius
The product of its mass and orbital speed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Law of Periods, also known as Kepler's Third Law, states that the square of the orbital period of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as: **T² ∝ a³**, where T is the orbital period and a is the semi-major axis.
 
• This law applies to planets, moons, and other celestial bodies orbiting a central body, such as the Sun or a star.
 
• The semi-major axis is the longest radius of an elliptical orbit, representing the average distance of the planet from the central body.
 
• Kepler's Third Law is derived from Newton's law of gravitation and provides a foundation for understanding orbital mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion:**

 
 
• 1st Law (Law of Ellipses): Planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus.
 
• 2nd Law (Law of Equal Areas): A line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time.
 
• 3rd Law (Law of Periods): The square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
 
 
• **Semi-Major Axis:**
 
 
• The semi-major axis is the average distance between the center of an orbiting body and the central body it orbits.
 
• For circular orbits, the semi-major axis is equivalent to the radius of the circle.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation:**
 
 
• Newton extended Kepler's laws by deriving them using his law of gravitation: F = G * (m1 * m2) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
• It explains how gravitational forces govern the motion of celestial objects.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Kepler's Third Law:**
 
 
• It is used in calculating orbital periods of planets, satellites, and space missions.
 
• It helps in understanding the dynamics of exoplanets and binary star systems.

questions.question: Which of Rutherford's experimental observations led him to conclude that the positive charge of an atom is concentrated in a very small region?

options.text: Electrons were found to orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels.
A very small fraction of a-particles rebounded almost backwards.
Most a-particles followed a straight path through the gold foil.
A small fraction of α-particles were deflected by small angles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A very small fraction of α-particles rebounded almost backwards.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rutherford's gold foil experiment involved the bombardment of a thin gold foil with α-particles (helium nuclei) to study atomic structure.
 
• Most α-particles passed through the foil undeflected, indicating that atoms are mostly empty space.
 
• A small fraction of α-particles were deflected at small angles, suggesting the presence of a positively charged center.
 
• A very tiny fraction of α-particles rebounded almost directly backward, leading Rutherford to conclude that the positive charge of the atom is concentrated in a very small, dense region, which he termed the nucleus.
 
• This observation provided experimental evidence for the nuclear model of the atom, replacing the earlier plum pudding model proposed by J.J. Thomson.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:** Conducted in 1909 by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden under the supervision of Ernest Rutherford, this experiment was pivotal in understanding atomic structure.
 
• **Nuclear Model of the Atom:** Proposed by Rutherford, it describes the atom as having a dense central nucleus containing protons, with electrons orbiting in the empty space surrounding it.
 
• **Plum Pudding Model:** An earlier atomic model proposed by J.J. Thomson, which suggested that electrons were embedded in a positively charged "pudding-like" substance. This model was disproved by Rutherford's experiment.
 
• **α-Particles:** Positively charged particles consisting of two protons and two neutrons, used as projectiles in the gold foil experiment.
 
• **Implications of Rutherford's Findings:** The discovery of the nucleus laid the foundation for the development of the modern quantum mechanical model of the atom and further studies on subatomic particles.

questions.question: The Western Coastal Plains are narrower compared to the Eastern Coastal Plains because:

options.text: They are bordered by the Western Ghats

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are bordered by the Western Ghats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Western Coastal Plains are narrower because they are bordered by the **Western Ghats**, a mountain range that runs parallel to the coast, leaving limited space for the plains.
 
• The proximity of the Western Ghats to the coast restricts the development of extensive coastal plains, unlike the Eastern Coastal Plains.
 
• In contrast, the Eastern Coastal Plains are wider as the Eastern Ghats are more discontinuous and distant from the coastline.
 
• The Western Coastal Plains span from Gujarat in the north to Kerala in the south, covering states like Maharashtra and Goa, with an average width of 50-100 km.
 
• These plains feature prominent geographical formations like lagoons, backwaters, and estuaries, shaped by the interaction of the terrain and the coastline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats**

 
 
• The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri Hills, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site recognized for their biodiversity.
 
• They influence the climate of the Western Coastal Plains by intercepting the southwest monsoon winds, causing heavy rainfall on the windward side.
 
• They are known for their steep slopes and dense forests, contributing to the narrowness of the plains.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Coastal Plains**
 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains lie between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal and are wider compared to their western counterpart.
 
• They feature river deltas formed by major rivers like the Ganga, Godavari, Krishna, and Mahanadi.
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains of India**
 
 
• India has two main coastal plains: the Western Coastal Plains and the Eastern Coastal Plains.
 
• The coastal plains are important for agriculture, fishing, tourism, and port development.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Influence**
 
 
• The physical geography of a region, including mountains and water bodies, plays a crucial role in shaping its landforms and ecosystems.
 
• The Western Ghats’ proximity to the Arabian Sea has resulted in unique features like estuaries and backwaters, such as Kerala's Vembanad Lake.

questions.question: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) as stipulated by the Constitution is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**550 members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is **550 members**, as per Article 81 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The allocation includes **530 members representing the states** and **20 members representing the Union Territories**.
 
• The President of India can also nominate **2 members from the Anglo-Indian community**, if deemed necessary (this provision was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019).
 
• Currently, the Lok Sabha has a sanctioned strength of **543 elected members** (530 from states and 13 from Union Territories).
 
• The Constitution specifies the upper limit of 552 members but allows flexibility in actual strength based on population and delimitation exercises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delimitation:**

 
 
• Delimitation refers to the act of redrawing boundaries of Lok Sabha and state legislative assembly constituencies based on population data.
 
• The Delimitation Commission is tasked with ensuring equitable representation across constituencies.
 
• The last delimitation exercise was conducted in 2002 based on the 2001 Census, and the next is expected after 2026.
 
 
 
• **104th Constitutional Amendment Act (2019):**
 
 
• This amendment abolished the provision of nominating 2 Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and state legislatures.
 
• Earlier, this was done to ensure representation for the Anglo-Indian community in India's legislative process.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha (Council of States):**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of the Indian Parliament with a maximum strength of 250 members.
 
• Out of these, 238 members are elected, and 12 members are nominated by the President for their expertise in literature, science, art, and social services.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary System of India:**
 
 
• India follows a bicameral parliamentary system consisting of the Lok Sabha (Lower House) and the Rajya Sabha (Upper House).
 
• The Lok Sabha represents the people of India, while the Rajya Sabha represents the states and Union Territories.

questions.question: Which recent mission by ISRO aims to study the Sun from the Lagrange point L1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aditya-L1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aditya-L1** is India's first solar mission, developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
 
• Its primary objective is to study the Sun, including the solar corona, chromosphere, and solar winds, from the strategic **Lagrange Point L1**.
 
• The mission was successfully launched on **September 2, 2023**, from Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, using the PSLV-C57 rocket.
 
• The spacecraft is equipped with seven scientific payloads designed to observe and analyze various aspects of the Sun.
 
• The positioning at the **Lagrange Point L1**, approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, provides uninterrupted observation of the Sun without any occultation or eclipses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lagrange Point L1**

 
 
• A Lagrange Point is a location in space where the gravitational forces of two large celestial bodies, like the Earth and Sun, balance the centripetal force felt by a smaller object.
 
• L1 is the point closest to the Sun, allowing continuous observation without disruptions caused by Earth's shadow.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Payloads on Aditya-L1**
 
 
• **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC):** Studies the solar corona and dynamics of coronal mass ejections.
 
• **Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT):** Observes the Sun's photosphere and chromosphere in near-ultraviolet wavelengths.
 
• **Aditya Solar Wind Particle Experiment (ASPEX):** Analyzes solar wind properties.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Solar Studies**
 
 
• Understanding solar phenomena like coronal mass ejections is crucial as they impact space weather and satellite operations.
 
• It helps in predicting geomagnetic storms that could disrupt communication systems and power grids on Earth.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Achievements**
 
 
• Aditya-L1 adds to ISRO’s legacy of pioneering space exploration missions, including Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan.
 
• It showcases India’s growing capabilities in conducting advanced scientific research and international collaborations.

questions.question: Name the state which is the largest producer of lignite coal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tamil Nadu is the **largest producer of lignite coal** in India, contributing significantly to the country’s lignite reserves and production.
 
• It is home to the **Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC)**, which is a major producer of lignite and operates large-scale mining and power generation activities in the state.
 
• The Neyveli region in Tamil Nadu is rich in lignite reserves and contains one of the **largest lignite mines** in India.
 
• Lignite coal, also known as brown coal, is primarily used for **power generation**, and Tamil Nadu’s lignite is utilized in thermal power plants in the region.
 
• As of recent data, Tamil Nadu contributes to approximately **50% of the total lignite production** in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lignite Coal:**

 
 
• Lignite is a type of sedimentary rock formed from naturally compressed peat and is considered the **lowest rank of coal** due to its lower heat content.
 
• It has a high moisture content and is primarily used for **electricity generation** in thermal power plants.
 
• India has significant lignite reserves, particularly in Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC):**
 
 
• NLC is a Central Public Sector Enterprise headquartered in Neyveli, Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is engaged in lignite mining and thermal power generation, contributing significantly to the energy sector of India.
 
• It operates one of the **largest opencast lignite mines** in the country.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Lignite:**
 
 
• Lignite is predominantly used for **thermal power generation** due to its lower energy content compared to higher-grade coal.
 
• It is also used in industries such as **cement, fertilizer, and iron & steel**, as well as for gasification and briquetting.
 
 
 
• **Other Leading States in Lignite Production:**
 
 
• Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir also contribute to India’s lignite production, though Tamil Nadu remains the leading producer.
 
• Rajasthan's **Barsingsar region** and Gujarat’s **Bhavnagar district** are notable for lignite mining activities.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler is credited with the establishment of the spy system in his empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire, is credited with establishing an extensive **spy system** to ensure efficient governance and internal security.
 
• This spy network was a part of the administrative framework suggested by his advisor **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, as outlined in the Arthashastra.
 
• The system comprised secret agents who worked undercover to gather intelligence on both internal and external matters.
 
• Spies were categorized based on their roles, such as **‘Sanstha’** (stationary informants) and **‘Sanchari’** (roving informants), to monitor various aspects of administration and society.
 
• The spy system played a critical role in safeguarding the empire from internal conspiracies and external threats, contributing to the stability of Chandragupta’s rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthashastra:**

 
 
• A comprehensive ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economics, and military strategy authored by Chanakya (Kautilya).
 
• It emphasizes the importance of a well-organized administrative system, including espionage, for efficient governance.
 
• The text is divided into 15 books, covering topics like diplomacy, law, taxation, and intelligence gathering.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya (Kautilya):**
 
 
• A renowned ancient Indian philosopher, economist, and political advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire and the formulation of its governance policies.
 
• Known for his strategic acumen and the compilation of the Arthashastra.
 
 
 
• **Spy System in Ancient India:**
 
 
• Ancient Indian rulers, including those of the Mauryan dynasty, used spies to gather intelligence on political, military, and economic matters.
 
• Spies often disguised themselves as ascetics, merchants, or commoners to blend into society and collect information.
 
• The system helped prevent rebellions, monitor officials, and manage foreign relations.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) was the first large-scale empire in Indian history, founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• It was marked by centralized administration, a well-organized bureaucracy, and military strength.
 
• Under rulers like Chandragupta and Ashoka, it became one of the most powerful empires in the ancient world.

questions.question: Which article provides for the appointment of Governors in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 155**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 155** of the Constitution of India provides for the appointment of Governors in Indian states.
 
• The Governor of a state is appointed by the **President of India** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• The appointment process ensures that the Governor serves as the representative of the Union Government in the state.
 
• The term of office for a Governor is normally **5 years**, but they serve at the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Governor's role is primarily ceremonial, but they hold powers as per the provisions of the Constitution, including executive, legislative, and discretionary powers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 154:** It vests the executive power of the state in the Governor, to be exercised directly or through officers subordinate to them.
 
• **Article 156:** It specifies the conditions of service and tenure of the Governor, stating they hold office at the pleasure of the President.
 
• **Federal Structure:** The appointment of Governors reflects India’s quasi-federal structure, where the Union Government has oversight over states through the Governor.
 
• **Role of the Governor:** The Governor acts as a constitutional head, ensuring the state government operates within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• **Discretionary Powers:** In certain situations, such as the dissolution of the state assembly or during a constitutional crisis, the Governor can act independently of the Council of Ministers.

questions.question: Which Pala ruler is known for founding the great Buddhist university at Vikramashila?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dharmapala**, the second ruler of the Pala dynasty, is credited with establishing the renowned Buddhist university at **Vikramashila**.
 
• Vikramashila University was one of the most important centers of Buddhist learning during medieval India, alongside Nalanda University.
 
• Dharmapala ruled from approximately **770–810 CE** and was a patron of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• The university attracted scholars from various parts of Asia and specialized in Tantric Buddhism.
 
• Dharmapala's contribution to education and Buddhism marked a golden age for learning in the Pala Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pala Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Pala dynasty ruled over Bihar, Bengal, and parts of Odisha from the 8th to the 12th century CE.
 
• The name "Pala" means protector, and all rulers of this dynasty had names ending with "Pala."
 
• The dynasty is known for its patronage of Buddhism and significant contributions to art, architecture, and education.
 
 
 
• **Vikramashila University:**
 
 
• Founded in the late 8th or early 9th century CE, it was located in modern-day Bhagalpur, Bihar.
 
• The university had over 100 teachers and thousands of students specializing in Buddhist philosophy, logic, grammar, and Tantric studies.
 
• It was destroyed during the invasions of Bakhtiyar Khilji in the 12th century.
 
 
 
• **Nalanda University:**
 
 
• Another prominent center of learning established in the 5th century CE in Bihar.
 
• It was a hub for Buddhist studies and attracted scholars from across Asia.
 
• It was supported by rulers like Harsha and several Pala kings, including Dharmapala.
 
 
 
• **Mahayana Buddhism:**
 
 
• A major branch of Buddhism that emphasizes the path of a Bodhisattva and compassion.
 
• Promoted by rulers of the Pala dynasty, including Dharmapala.
 
• Its teachings influenced the curriculum of Vikramashila University.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the chronological order of human development during gestation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zygote - Embryo - Fetus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Zygote** is the first stage of human development, formed after the fusion of the male and female gametes (sperm and ovum) during fertilization.
 
• The **zygote undergoes mitotic divisions** (cleavage) to form a multicellular structure called the **embryo**.
 
• The **embryo** is the early developmental stage where cells differentiate and organs start forming, typically lasting until the 8th week of gestation.
 
• After 8 weeks, the developing human is referred to as a **fetus**, where growth and further development of organs occur until birth.
 
• The chronological order of human development during gestation is: **Zygote → Embryo → Fetus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zygote:**

 
 
• A single-celled structure formed by the fusion of sperm and ovum during fertilization.
 
• It contains the complete genetic material (46 chromosomes) necessary for human development.
 
 
 
• **Embryo:**
 
 
• The developing organism from the 2nd week to the 8th week of pregnancy.
 
• Critical processes such as cell division, differentiation, and organogenesis occur during this stage.
 
 
 
• **Fetus:**
 
 
• The stage from the 9th week of gestation until birth.
 
• During this stage, the body systems develop further, and the fetus grows in size and weight.
 
 
 
• **Gestation Period:**
 
 
• The average duration of human pregnancy is approximately 40 weeks (280 days) from the last menstrual period.
 
• It is divided into three trimesters, each focusing on specific aspects of fetal development.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Thiru K. Kamaraj on his birth anniversary. He is remembered for his contributions to which of the following areas?

options.text: Freedom struggle and social welfare governance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Freedom struggle and social welfare governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thiru K. Kamaraj, popularly known as the "Kingmaker," was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and politician from Tamil Nadu.
 
• He played a vital role in India's freedom struggle, participating in movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement and the Quit India Movement.
 
• Kamaraj was instrumental in introducing mid-day meals and free education in Tamil Nadu, laying the foundation for social welfare governance.
 
• His efforts significantly improved literacy rates and access to education for the underprivileged in Tamil Nadu.
 
• He served as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu from 1954 to 1963 and focused on developmental policies, including rural electrification and industrialization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, this movement aimed at boycotting British goods, titles, and institutions.
 
• Kamaraj joined the movement and actively participated in protests against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:**
 
 
• Kamaraj introduced the mid-day meal scheme in Tamil Nadu during his tenure as Chief Minister.
 
• It aimed at improving school enrollment and reducing dropout rates among underprivileged children.
 
 
 
• **Rural Electrification:**
 
 
• Kamaraj prioritized electrification of villages in Tamil Nadu, boosting agricultural productivity and rural development.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• He is remembered as a leader who remained committed to social welfare and development.

questions.question: What was the primary impact of the 'License Raj' system on industrial growth in India before 1991?

options.text: It created entry barriers, hindered expansion, and fostered inefficiency.
It led to efficient resource allocation and increased competition.
It ensured balanced regional development and prevented monopolies.
It promoted rapid industrial diversification and innovation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It created entry barriers, hindered expansion, and fostered inefficiency.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'License Raj' system, implemented in India from 1947 to 1991, required businesses to obtain multiple licenses and permits, creating significant entry barriers for new firms.
 
• This system limited industrial expansion, as obtaining approvals for capacity increases or diversification was a lengthy and bureaucratic process.
 
• It fostered inefficiency by promoting monopolistic tendencies, as established players faced little competition due to the restrictive licensing regime.
 
• The system discouraged innovation and entrepreneurship, as businesses focused more on compliance with regulations rather than improving productivity or technology.
 
• Overall, the 'License Raj' hindered industrial growth and economic dynamism, contributing to India's slower growth rates during this period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **License Raj:**

 
 
• It refers to the elaborate system of licenses, permits, and quotas that governed India's industrial sector from independence until the economic liberalization of 1991.
 
• The term was coined to describe the overregulated economy, which was heavily controlled by government intervention.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Industrial Growth:**
 
 
• Industries faced high compliance costs and delays, which discouraged private investment.
 
• The lack of competition under the License Raj led to suboptimal resource allocation and stagnation in technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Economic Liberalization of 1991:**
 
 
• The reforms of 1991 dismantled the License Raj, opening up the economy to market forces and foreign investment.
 
• The focus shifted to deregulation, privatization, and liberalization, allowing faster industrial growth and global integration.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures:**
 
 
• The economic policies of Jawaharlal Nehru and subsequent leaders institutionalized the License Raj, while reforms were led by then-Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh under the leadership of PM P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1991.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary objective of a government's fiscal policy?

options.text: To control the money supply and interest rates.
To promote international trade and maintain a favorable balance of payments.
To influence aggregate demand and economic activity through government spending and taxation.
To regulate the stock market and financial institutions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To influence aggregate demand and economic activity through government spending and taxation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fiscal policy is a tool used by governments to influence a nation's economy by adjusting **government spending** and **taxation policies**.
 
• The primary objective of fiscal policy is to manage **aggregate demand** to achieve macroeconomic goals such as economic growth, price stability, and employment generation.
 
• Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing government spending or reducing taxes to stimulate economic activity during a slowdown or recession.
 
• Contractionary fiscal policy, on the other hand, involves reducing government spending or increasing taxes to control inflation during an economic boom.
 
• Fiscal policy works in tandem with monetary policy to ensure overall economic stability and growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aggregate Demand:**

 
 
• It refers to the total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given overall price level and in a given time period.
 
• Fiscal policy impacts aggregate demand directly through changes in government spending and indirectly through taxation.
 
 
 
• **Components of Fiscal Policy:**
 
 
• **Government Spending:** Includes expenditures on infrastructure, education, healthcare, etc., which directly influence economic activity.
 
• **Taxation:** Adjusting tax rates affects disposable income, consumer spending, and business investment.
 
 
 
• **Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• Fiscal policy leverages the multiplier effect, where an initial change in spending leads to a greater overall impact on the economy.
 
• This is particularly significant in times of economic downturn when stimulating demand is crucial.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• It occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed the revenue it generates, excluding money from borrowings.
 
• A controlled fiscal deficit ensures that fiscal policy remains sustainable in the long run.
 
 
 
• **Automatic Stabilizers:**
 
 
• These are economic policies and programs, such as progressive taxation and unemployment benefits, that automatically adjust to stabilize an economy without explicit intervention.
 
• They help reduce the intensity of economic fluctuations.

questions.question: In which decade did India experience a negative growth rate in population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1911-1921**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decade 1911-1921 is the only period in Indian history where the population growth rate was negative, registering a decline of -0.31%.
 
• The negative growth rate was primarily caused by the widespread outbreak of the **Spanish Flu pandemic** (1918–1920), which claimed millions of lives in India.
 
• Other contributing factors included severe famines, widespread poverty, and poor healthcare infrastructure during British colonial rule.
 
• This decline was recorded in the 1921 Census, which marked a significant demographic anomaly in Indian population trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spanish Flu Pandemic:**

 
 
• The Spanish Flu pandemic of 1918–1920 was one of the deadliest global pandemics, killing an estimated 50 million people worldwide.
 
• India was heavily impacted, with around 12–17 million deaths, accounting for about 5% of the population at the time.
 
• Poor sanitation, lack of medical care, and malnutrition exacerbated the death toll in India.
 
 
 
• **Famines in British India:**
 
 
• Frequent famines during British colonial rule further contributed to population decline.
 
• Major famines included the Bengal Famine of 1918 and others caused by inadequate food distribution and exploitative policies.
 
 
 
• **India's Census System:**
 
 
• The census of India began in 1872 under British rule, with systematic enumeration starting from 1881.
 
• The 1921 Census was notable for recording the negative population growth rate and was referred to as the "Demographic Divide."
 
 
 
• **Population Growth Trends:**
 
 
• India's population growth rate has been positive since 1921 due to improvements in healthcare, food supply, and overall living conditions.
 
• The 1921 Census is considered the watershed moment in India's demographic history, marking the transition towards sustained population growth.

questions.question: How can NISAR provide valuable information for understanding the relationship between fluid injection and earthquake?

options.text: By tracking changes in ground surface elevation associated with pumping and injection
By measuring seismic activity in real time
By analyzing satellite imagery of earthquake damage

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By tracking changes in ground surface elevation associated with pumping and injection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar)** is designed to use advanced radar imaging techniques to detect minute changes in Earth's surface, including those caused by fluid injection or extraction.
 
• By measuring **ground surface deformation** over time, NISAR can provide critical insights into subsurface activities associated with activities like wastewater injection or geothermal energy extraction.
 
• Ground uplift or subsidence caused by fluid injection can be **early indicators of stress changes in the Earth's crust**, which are linked to induced seismicity.
 
• NISAR’s ability to monitor ground elevation changes with **centimeter-level precision** on a global scale makes it a valuable tool for earthquake research and mitigation strategies.
 
• Such data helps scientists establish correlations between **human-induced activities** (like fluid injection) and **earthquake patterns**, improving risk assessment models.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Induced Seismicity:**

 
 
• This refers to earthquakes caused by human activities such as mining, reservoir-induced seismicity (from dams), or fluid injection during processes like fracking and geothermal energy extraction.
 
• It is often linked to changes in subsurface stress due to the movement or injection of fluids.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):**
 
 
• SAR is a remote sensing technology that uses radar to create high-resolution images of Earth’s surface.
 
• It is effective in all weather conditions, day or night, making it ideal for continuous monitoring of surface changes.
 
 
 
• **How NISAR Works:**
 
 
• NISAR uses two radar frequencies (L-band and S-band) to measure Earth's surface deformation with unparalleled accuracy.
 
• The mission, a joint collaboration between NASA and ISRO, aims to monitor environmental changes, natural disasters, and anthropogenic impacts.
 
 
 
• **Fluid Injection and Earthquakes:**
 
 
• Activities like wastewater injection or hydraulic fracturing can increase pore pressure in rocks, potentially triggering fault slip and seismic activity.
 
• Monitoring ground deformation helps identify areas at risk of induced seismicity.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake Risk Mitigation:**
 
 
• Using data from tools like NISAR, scientists can develop strategies to minimize risks associated with human-induced seismic activity.
 
• Such insights aid in designing policies for the safe regulation of activities like fluid injection.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the broader geopolitical shift triggered by the decisive defeat of the Nawab of Carnatic's forces in their confrontation with European powers?

options.text: It revealed systemic vulnerabilities in native military structures, prompting European companies to transition from trade to political thegemony.
It disillusioned European companies, resulting in a strategic withdrawal from inland military affairs.
It consolidated indigenous authority, forcing European traders into commercial treaties under local oversight.
It established a stable dual-administrative system between Indian principalities and foreign chartered companies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: It revealed systemic vulnerabilities in native military structures, prompting European companies to transition from trade to political hegemony.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The defeat of the Nawab of Carnatic's forces in confrontations with European powers exposed significant weaknesses in the organizational and technological capabilities of native Indian armies.
 
• European companies, like the British East India Company, capitalized on these vulnerabilities to expand their influence beyond trade and establish political dominance over regional powers.
 
• This event marked a pivotal shift from purely commercial ventures to the adoption of military and administrative roles by European chartered companies in India.
 
• It set a precedent for the systematic subjugation of Indian principalities, laying the groundwork for colonial rule and the eventual consolidation of British authority in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The shift was characterized by the establishment of fortified settlements, alliances with local rulers, and direct military interventions to secure territorial control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Carnatic Wars:**

 
 
• A series of military conflicts in South India during the 18th century between European powers (primarily British and French) and their allied Indian rulers.
 
• These wars highlighted the growing intervention of European companies in Indian political affairs.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Native Military Systems:**
 
 
• Indian armies lacked the advanced weaponry, training, and discipline possessed by European forces.
 
• Native forces were often fragmented due to regional rivalries, limiting their ability to resist European expansion effectively.
 
 
 
• **European Companies’ Transition to Political Power:**
 
 
• Initially focused on trade, companies like the British East India Company began leveraging military superiority to dominate Indian territories.
 
• This transition marked the beginning of colonial administration and exploitation in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Society:**
 
 
• The defeat and subsequent European dominance disrupted traditional political structures and economic systems in the region.
 
• It also led to the gradual erosion of indigenous authority and the establishment of foreign-controlled governance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why certain regions exhibit high population density?

options.text: Regions offering fertile land, favorable climates, abundant natural resources, and robust economic opportunities are more likely to have high population densities.
High population density is predominantly found in areas with poor infrastructure and limited access to essential services.
Regions with limited natural resources tend to have Areas with scarce natural resources have higher population concentrations because of greater competition for few materials.
Areas characterized by mountainous terrain and arid climates often support dense populations because of their challenging living conditions.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regions with high population density are typically characterized by **fertile land**, which supports agricultural activities and sustains large populations.
 
• **Favorable climates**, such as temperate or tropical climates, make living conditions more conducive for humans and agriculture, attracting more settlers.
 
• Availability of **abundant natural resources** (e.g., water, minerals, forests) supports economic activities, leading to population concentration in such areas.
 
• Regions with **robust economic opportunities**, such as urban centers, attract migration due to better job prospects, education, and infrastructure.
 
• Historical factors, such as the development of early civilizations in river valleys like the Nile, Ganges, or Yangtze, demonstrate the role of fertile land and water resources in promoting high population densities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:** It is the number of people living per unit area, typically measured in people per square kilometer.
 
• **Urbanization:** Urban areas often have higher population densities due to industrialization, better infrastructure, and job availability.
 
• **Carrying Capacity:** The maximum population size that an environment can sustain indefinitely, given the available resources such as food, water, and shelter.
 
• **Natural Resources:** The availability of resources like rivers, forests, and minerals contributes significantly to population distribution patterns.
 
• **Climatic Factors:** Moderate climates (neither too hot nor too cold) are preferred by humans, whereas extreme climates such as deserts or polar regions have lower population densities.

questions.question: What is the role of the Speaker in the case of a tie during voting in the Lok Sabha?

options.text: Refers the decision to the President

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**casting vote**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the **casting vote**, which is used only in the case of a tie during voting in the House.
 
• This casting vote is exercised to break the deadlock and ensure a decision is made.
 
• The Speaker's casting vote is intended to preserve neutrality and maintain parliamentary procedures.
 
• It is exercised sparingly and only when the voting results are evenly split (e.g., 50-50).
 
• The casting vote is a constitutional privilege granted under **Article 100(1)** of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speaker of the Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament in India.
 
• The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha after each general election or when the position is vacant.
 
• The primary duty of the Speaker is to maintain order and decorum during the proceedings of the House.
 
 
 
• **Article 100 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 100(1) states that all questions in the House shall be decided by a majority of votes.
 
• It empowers the Speaker to cast a vote in case of a tie.
 
 
 
• **Neutral Role of the Speaker:**
 
 
• The Speaker is expected to remain impartial and uphold the dignity of the House.
 
• Even while exercising the casting vote, the Speaker ensures procedural fairness.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Casting Vote:**
 
 
• The casting vote ensures that the legislative process is not stalled due to a tie.
 
• It reflects the Speaker’s responsibility to facilitate decision-making in the House.

questions.question: Which government scheme aims to phase out unfit and polluting vehicles from India's roads to reduce emissions and boost automotive industry recycling?

• Promotion of recycling industries, creating economic and environmental benefits.

questions.question:
Which constitutional features in India are linked to the Australian Constitution?

A) Freedom of trade and commerce

B) Joint sitting of the two Houses

c) Federal structure with strong Centre

D) Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and B both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Two significant constitutional features in India are influenced by the Australian Constitution: **freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse (Article 301)** and the **provision for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament**.
 
• The principle of **freedom of trade and commerce** ensures economic integration and unification, preventing states from imposing restrictions on inter-state trade.
 
• The **joint sitting mechanism**, mentioned in Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, facilitates the resolution of deadlocks on legislative bills between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Both features were directly adopted from the Australian Constitution, where similar provisions exist to ensure economic uniformity and legislative efficiency.
 
• These provisions highlight the influence of global constitutional practices on the framing of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freedom of Trade and Commerce**

 
 
• Article 301 of the Indian Constitution ensures the freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the country.
 
• This principle prevents discrimination between states and promotes economic unity.
 
• It is influenced by Section 92 of the Australian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Joint Sitting of Parliament**
 
 
• Article 108 of the Indian Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses in case of disagreements over legislative bills.
 
• This provision is inspired by Section 57 of the Australian Constitution, which resolves legislative deadlocks through a joint sitting.
 
 
 
• **Federal Features with a Strong Centre**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution adopts a federal structure with unitary bias, influenced by Canada rather than Australia.
 
• Australia follows a "cooperative federalism" model, distinct from India's centralized federalism.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**
 
 
• Article 143 of the Indian Constitution provides for the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
 
• This feature is influenced by the Government of India Act, 1935, rather than the Australian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following initiatives was launched by the BRICS countries?

__
 
• The New Development Bank (NDB) was established by the BRICS nations—**Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**—in July 2014 during the 6th BRICS Summit held in Fortaleza, Brazil.
 
• The primary objective of the NDB is to **mobilize resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects** in BRICS and other emerging economies. 
 
• The bank started its operations in 2015, with its headquarters located in** Shanghai, China**. 
 
• Each member country has an equal shareholding in the NDB, promoting **equality and inclusivity in decision-making** within the bank.
 
• In addition to financing projects, the NDB aims to strengthen cooperation among BRICS nations and provide an alternative to traditional financial institutions such as the IMF and the World Bank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS Overview:**

 
 
• BRICS is an acronym for an economic bloc consisting of five emerging economies: Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa.
 
• It was officially formed in 2006 to promote cooperation in economic, political, and social development.
 
• BRICS countries collectively account for about 40% of the world’s population and over 25% of the global GDP.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the NDB:**
 
 
• The NDB aims to **reduce reliance on traditional Western-led financial institutions** like the IMF and World Bank.
 
• It focuses on sustainable development projects, including renewable energy, transportation, and urban development.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanism:**
 
 
• Each BRICS country contributes equally to the NDB’s initial capital of $50 billion.
 
• The bank also raises funds through bond issuance in local currencies to support its lending operations.
 
 
 
• **Achievements:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• India adopted the concept of Five-Year Plans from the Soviet Union to achieve planned economic development.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture, irrigation, and energy.
 
• The Planning Commission was responsible for designing and implementing these plans until its dissolution in 2014, when it was replaced by NITI Aayog.

questions.question: What was the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee-Il regarding public sector banks?

Increase government ownership in public sector banks
Merge and consolidate public sector banks

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Narasimham Committee-II, constituted in 1998, recommended the **merger and consolidation of public sector banks** to create fewer but stronger banks.
 
• The aim was to improve **operational efficiency**, enhance competitiveness, and address the challenges posed by globalization and financial sector reforms.
 
• The committee suggested **reducing the number of public sector banks** to around 3-4 large banks with international reach and a few regional banks.

• The second committee emphasized structural reforms, including consolidation, governance improvements, and non-performing asset (NPA) management.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects the scarcity problem in economics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limited resources and unlimited wants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The scarcity problem in economics arises due to the fundamental concept of **unlimited human wants** and **limited resources** available to fulfill those wants.
 
• Scarcity forces individuals and societies to make choices about how to allocate resources efficiently to satisfy competing needs and desires.
 
• It highlights the necessity of prioritizing and making trade-offs, as resources such as land, labor, capital, and raw materials are finite.
 
• Scarcity is the driving force behind key economic concepts such as **opportunity cost**, production possibility curves, and the allocation of goods and services.
 
• This problem is universal and affects individuals, businesses, and governments, leading to the study of economics as a discipline to address resource allocation efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scarcity:** A fundamental economic problem referring to the gap between limited resources and theoretically unlimited wants.
 
• **Opportunity Cost:** The value of the next best alternative foregone when a choice is made due to resource limitations.
 
• **Production Possibility Curve (PPC):** A graphical representation of different combinations of two goods or services that can be produced with fixed resources and technology.
 
• **Resource Allocation:** The process of distributing scarce resources among various uses to meet the needs of individuals and society.
 
• **Factors of Production:** The inputs used to produce goods and services, including land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship.

questions.question: If a person view the Earth from above the North Pole, he will observe that the Earth rotates in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anti-clockwise**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When observed from above the North Pole, the Earth rotates in an **anti-clockwise direction**, which is consistent with its west-to-east rotational motion.
 
• The Earth completes one full rotation approximately every **24 hours**, causing the alternation of day and night.
 
• This rotational direction is referred to as **prograde rotation**, as it aligns with the orbit of most planets in the Solar System.
 
• The anti-clockwise rotation is a result of the conservation of angular momentum from the time of the Earth's formation in the Solar Nebula.
 
• As a consequence of this rotation, celestial objects such as the Sun and stars appear to rise in the east and set in the west.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direction of Earth's Rotation:**

 
 
• The Earth's rotation is defined as **counterclockwise (anti-clockwise)** when viewed from the North Pole.
 
• Conversely, when viewed from the South Pole, the rotation appears to be clockwise.
 
 
 
• **Axial Tilt and Seasons:**
 
 
• The Earth is tilted at an angle of approximately **23.5 degrees** to its orbital plane, which leads to the variation in seasons.
 
• This tilt, combined with the anti-clockwise rotation, affects the distribution of sunlight across the planet.
 
 
 
• **Time Zones and Rotation:**
 
 
• The Earth's rotation results in the division of the globe into **24 time zones**.
 
• Each time zone corresponds to 15 degrees of longitude, representing one hour of time.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Angular Momentum:**
 
 
• Earth's rotation direction is a consequence of the **conservation of angular momentum** during the formation of the Solar System.
 
• This principle ensures that the rotational characteristics of the early solar nebula were preserved in the motion of planets.
 
 
 
• **Prograde vs. Retrograde Rotation:**
 
 
• Most planets, including Earth, have a **prograde rotation** (rotating anti-clockwise when viewed from above their north poles).
 
• However, Venus and Uranus exhibit **retrograde rotation**, rotating in the opposite direction.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the extent of executive power of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 73**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 73** of the Indian Constitution specifies the extent of the executive power of the Union.
 
• It states that the executive power of the Union shall extend to matters on which Parliament has the power to make laws.
 
• The scope also includes exercising rights, authority, and jurisdiction conferred on the Union by any treaty or agreement.
 
• This Article ensures that the Union government can act on subjects mentioned in the Union List and subjects under its jurisdiction.
 
• It emphasizes the exclusive domain of the Union’s executive power, distinguishing it from the powers of the states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Executive Power:**

 
 
• The Union executive power is executed by the President as per Article 53 of the Constitution.
 
• The President exercises these powers directly or through officers subordinate to him, following constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Division of Powers:**
 
 
• The Constitution divides legislative and executive powers between the Union and State governments through the Seventh Schedule.
 
• The Union List contains subjects where the Union has exclusive authority, while the State List and Concurrent List outline other areas of jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Executive Power in Treaties:**
 
 
• Article 73 extends the Union’s executive power to obligations under international treaties or agreements.
 
• This ensures compliance with external commitments that fall within the Union’s jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Limitations on State Power:**
 
 
• Article 73 restricts state governments from interfering in matters exclusively under Union control.
 
• This creates a clear separation of powers and avoids overlap in governance.

questions.question: The Battle of Samugarh was fought between Aurangzeb and which Mughal prince?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dara Shikoh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Samugarh was fought on **29 May 1658** near Agra during the Mughal succession war.
 
• It was a decisive battle between **Aurangzeb** and his elder brother **Dara Shikoh**, both sons of Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• Dara Shikoh led an army to defend his claim to the throne but was defeated by Aurangzeb’s more disciplined forces.
 
• Aurangzeb's victory in the battle enabled him to capture Agra and imprison their father, Shah Jahan, solidifying his claim to the Mughal throne.
 
• Dara Shikoh was eventually captured and executed on Aurangzeb’s orders in 1659.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dara Shikoh:**

 
 
• Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of Shah Jahan and considered his father’s preferred successor.
 
• He was known for his interest in art, philosophy, and religious syncretism, particularly his efforts to bridge Hindu and Islamic traditions.
 
• His writings include the translation of the Upanishads into Persian, titled *Sirr-e-Akbar* (The Great Secret).
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, is known for his military prowess and expansion of the empire.
 
• He was a staunch follower of Islamic orthodoxy and implemented policies that were often seen as anti-Hindu.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Mughal Empire but also sowed seeds of its eventual decline.
 
 
 
• **The Mughal Succession Wars:**
 
 
• The Mughal Empire followed no fixed succession system, often leading to violent struggles between heirs.
 
• Key battles like Samugarh reflected the intense rivalry among Shah Jahan’s sons: Dara Shikoh, Aurangzeb, Murad Baksh, and Shuja.
 
 
 
• **Samugarh:**
 
 
• Samugarh is located near Agra and has historical significance due to the battle fought there.
 
• The battle demonstrated Aurangzeb’s superior military strategy and discipline under his general Mir Jumla.

questions.question: Which Indian plateau is formed primarily by volcanic activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau in western and southern India and is known for its **volcanic origin.**
 
• This plateau was primarily formed due to the **Deccan Traps volcanic activity** that occurred around 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period.
 
• The Deccan Traps consist of **basaltic lava flows** spread across an area of around 500,000 square kilometers.
 
• It is one of the largest volcanic features on Earth and is known for its **step-like formation** of hardened lava layers.
 
• The plateau covers parts of states such as **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deccan Traps**:

 
 
• The term "trap" is derived from the Swedish word "trappa," meaning stairs, due to the step-like appearance of the rock formations.
 
• The volcanic activity is linked to the breakup of the Gondwana supercontinent and the impact of the Reunion hotspot.
 
• The lava flows of the Deccan Traps are primarily composed of basalt, a type of igneous rock.
 
 
 
• **Geological significance of the Deccan Plateau**:
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is rich in minerals such as iron ore, manganese, and bauxite.
 
• The black soil in the region, known as **regur soil**, is highly fertile and suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Climatic influence**:
 
 
• The plateau has a semi-arid to tropical climate, with distinct wet and dry seasons.
 
• It plays a crucial role in shaping the weather patterns of southern India.
 
 
 
• **Ecological importance**:
 
 
• The plateau hosts a wide variety of flora and fauna, including several endemic species.
 
• It is home to significant biodiversity hotspots such as the **Western Ghats**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question:

Statement 1: The Mridangam is a melodic percussion instrument used to outline the raga.

Statement 2: Nadaswaram is a double-reed instrument traditionally played in temples and weddings.
questions.solution:

• **Statement 2 is correct:** The Nadaswaram is a double-reed wind instrument widely used in South Indian classical music, especially in temples and during auspicious occasions such as weddings.
 
• The Nadaswaram is often considered an auspicious instrument, symbolizing traditional and cultural heritage in South Indian ceremonies.
 
• The Mridangam, though crucial in Carnatic music performances, is primarily a rhythm-providing instrument and does not define the melodic structure of the raga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mridangam:**

• The Mridangam is tuned to the tonic note of the vocalist or lead instrumentalist and is played with the hands.
 
• It is an integral part of Carnatic music concerts, providing complex rhythmic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Nadaswaram:**
 
 
• It is one of the loudest non-brass acoustic instruments and is made of wood, often from the aacha or blackwood tree.
 
• The instrument has a conical bore, which helps produce a rich, resonant tone.
 
• It is traditionally accompanied by the Thavil, a percussion instrument.
 
 
 
• **Raga in Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Raga is a melodic framework that defines the mood and structure of a composition in Carnatic music.
 
• It is elaborated using melodic instruments such as the violin, flute, or veena, and through vocal improvisation.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• A classical music tradition of South India with a rich history and theoretical foundation.

questions.question: As per Chapter I (Preliminary) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which of the following is not applicable under the Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Affidavits submitted before court officer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Indian Evidence Act, 2023), primarily governs the rules of evidence admissible in courts of law.
 
• Under Chapter I (Preliminary), the Act does not apply to affidavits submitted before court officers as they are governed by separate procedural laws.
 
• Affidavits are considered written sworn statements of fact and are regulated under the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other applicable laws.
 
• The Act explicitly applies to proceedings before judicial courts, including civil and criminal courts, but excludes certain quasi-judicial and administrative proceedings.
 
• Trials before Military Courts (Court-Martial) are also explicitly excluded from the purview of this Act under the provisions of specific military laws such as the Army Act, 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Terminology of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam:**

 
 
• "Evidence" includes oral evidence (testimony of witnesses) and documentary evidence (written or recorded materials).
 
• "Fact in issue" refers to the primary points of dispute between parties in a legal proceeding.
 
• "Relevance" determines which facts are admissible as evidence in a particular case.
 
 
 
• **Exclusion of Certain Proceedings:**
 
 
• Military Court proceedings are excluded under the Indian Evidence Act and are governed by military-specific laws.
 
• Affidavits and administrative proceedings are governed by procedural and administrative law, not the Evidence Act.
 
 
 
• **Military Courts (Court-Martial):**
 
 
• Military courts operate under the Army Act, Air Force Act, or Navy Act, depending on the armed force concerned.
 
• They have their own rules of evidence and procedures, distinct from the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.
 
 
 
• **Civil vs. Criminal Trials:**
 
 
• Civil trials deal with disputes between individuals or organizations (e.g., property disputes).
 
• Criminal trials involve offenses against the state and are prosecuted by the government (e.g., theft, murder).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908:**
 
 
• The Code governs the procedural aspects of civil cases, including the submission of affidavits.
 
• It provides guidelines for the admissibility and format of affidavits in civil proceedings.

questions.question: Which classical dance form is associated with the state of Kerala ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, India.
 
• It is renowned for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and expressive gestures, which depict themes from Hindu epics like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.
 
• The dance form combines music, vocal performances, and hand gestures (**mudras**) to convey stories and emotions.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed during the night and can last for several hours, showcasing Kerala's rich cultural heritage.
 
• Renowned for its vibrant storytelling, Kathakali is recognized globally as one of the most visually impressive forms of Indian classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Costumes and Makeup:**

 
 
• Costumes are elaborate, featuring a large headgear, colorful attire, and intricate facial makeup.
 
• Facial makeup uses natural pigments and colors to emphasize characters' traits—green for noble characters, red for villains, etc.
 
 
 
• **Music and Instruments:**
 
 
• Kathakali performances are accompanied by traditional instruments like **chenda** (drum), **idakka**, and **shankh** (conch).
 
• Vocal music plays a crucial role, with lyrics often sung in Malayalam or Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Training and Preparation:**
 
 
• Kathakali artists undergo rigorous training, including mastering **kalaripayattu** (traditional martial art) for flexibility and stamina.
 
• The training includes learning complex gestures and expressions to convey emotions effectively.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Kathakali originated in the 17th century and is believed to have evolved from earlier temple art forms such as **Krishnanattam**.
 
• The dance form represents Kerala's cultural identity and is often performed during festivals and cultural events.

questions.question: What does a lower GPI score indicate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Higher level of peace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Global Peace Index (GPI) measures the relative peacefulness of nations and regions based on various indicators such as societal safety, security, and levels of conflict.
 
• A lower GPI score signifies a higher level of peace, indicating minimal violence, conflict, and political instability in the evaluated region.
 
• Countries with lower GPI scores often exhibit strong governance, higher levels of economic stability, and effective law enforcement practices.
 
• GPI uses metrics like the number of deaths from conflict, perceptions of criminality, and military expenditure to calculate peace levels.
 
• According to the latest GPI report (2023), Iceland continues to rank as the most peaceful country globally, maintaining its low GPI score.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Peace Index (GPI):**

 
 
• The Global Peace Index is published annually by the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP).
 
• It ranks 163 countries based on 23 qualitative and quantitative indicators divided into three domains: ongoing conflict, safety and security, and militarization.
 
• The GPI serves as a comprehensive framework to understand global peace trends and their economic impact.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Peace on Socio-Economic Development:**
 
 
• Countries with higher levels of peace tend to have better education systems, healthcare facilities, and economic growth.
 
• Peaceful nations typically attract more foreign investments, contributing to sustainable development and reducing poverty.
 
 
 
• **Notable GPI Trends (2023):**
 
 
• Iceland remains the most peaceful country for over a decade, followed by New Zealand and Ireland.
 
• Afghanistan ranks as the least peaceful country due to ongoing conflict and instability.

Consider the following statements about Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves:

1. These caves are near Bhubaneswar and were meant for Jain monks.

2. All caves are shaped like flowers and are carved from independent boulders.

3. Each cave has multiple shrines dedicated to different Buddhist deities.

Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves** are a group of rock-cut caves located near Bhubaneswar in Odisha, India.
 
• The caves were primarily **meant for Jain monks**, serving as their dwellings and meditation spaces.
 
• These caves are believed to have been commissioned by King Kharavela of the Mahameghavahana dynasty in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• The caves are not shaped like flowers or carved from independent boulders; they are instead **excavated from the hillside**.
 
• While primarily Jain in nature, the caves do not have multiple shrines dedicated to Buddhist deities, making statements 2 and 3 incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jain Influence:**

 
 
• The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves are among the earliest Jain rock-cut architecture in India.
 
• They reflect the ascetic practices and the art patronage of Jainism during the rule of King Kharavela.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Highlights:**
 
 
• The most notable caves include the **Hathi Gumpha (Elephant Cave)**, which has inscriptions detailing King Kharavela's reign, and the **Rani Gumpha (Queen's Cave)**, known for its elaborate carvings.
 
• The caves are adorned with sculptures of Jain Tirthankaras and scenes depicting Jain mythology.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The inscriptions in the caves provide valuable insights into the socio-political and religious landscape of ancient Odisha.
 
• They highlight the spread of Jainism and its integration into local culture during the early Common Era.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Preservation:**
 
 
• The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves are a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
 
• The site attracts tourists and scholars interested in ancient Indian art, history, and religion.

Consider the following statements:

1. A solar eclipse- The Moon caste a shadow on Earth when it comes between the Sun and Earth.

2. A lunar eclipse- During the new moon phase, the Moon passes through the Earth's shadow.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) 1 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1** is correct: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting its shadow on Earth.
 
• **Statement 2** is incorrect: A lunar eclipse occurs during the full moon phase, not the new moon phase, when the Moon passes through Earth's shadow.
 
• During a solar eclipse, the Sun appears partially or completely obscured as seen from Earth due to the Moon's shadow.
 
• Lunar eclipses happen only when the Sun, Earth, and Moon align perfectly in a straight line, with Earth in the middle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar Eclipse:**

 
 
• Occurs during the new moon phase when the Moon blocks sunlight from reaching Earth.
 
• The three types of solar eclipses are total, partial, and annular.
 
• A total solar eclipse occurs when the Moon completely covers the Sun, casting a shadow on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Lunar Eclipse:**
 
 
• Occurs during the full moon phase when Earth casts its shadow on the Moon.
 
• The two types of lunar eclipses are total and partial, depending on the extent of the Earth's shadow covering the Moon.
 
• The reddish appearance of the Moon during a total lunar eclipse is due to Earth's atmosphere scattering sunlight, known as the "blood moon" effect.
 
 
 
• **Phases of the Moon:** The Moon goes through eight phases (new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent) in its monthly cycle.
 
• **Alignment (Syzygy):** A solar or lunar eclipse can only occur during syzygy, when the Sun, Moon, and Earth align in a straight line.
 
• **Umbra and Penumbra:**
 
 
• The umbra is the darkest part of the shadow where the Sun is completely blocked.
 
• The penumbra is the lighter shadow where the Sun is only partially obscured.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of developing Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) in agriculture ?

• They are modified to enhance **nutritional profiles**, such as adding vitamins or nutrients to crops like rice and maize.

__
 
• The first Commonwealth Games were held in **Hamilton, Canada**, from **August 16 to August 23, 1930**.
 
• The event was initially called the **British Empire Games** and later renamed to Commonwealth Games in 1950.
 
• A total of **11 nations** participated in the inaugural games, featuring **6 sports** and 59 events.
 
• The vision for the games was conceived by **Melville Marks Robinson**, a Canadian sports administrator.
 
• Hamilton, Canada, provided a $30,000 fund to cover travel expenses for competitors from participating countries.

• It is held every **four years**, with participation limited to Commonwealth member countries.
 
• The games promote **friendship and cooperation** among member nations through sports.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Games**
 
 
• The name transitioned from the British Empire Games (1930–1950) to the British Empire and Commonwealth Games (1954–1966), the British Commonwealth Games (1970–1974), and finally the Commonwealth Games (from 1978).
 
• Women’s participation expanded significantly over time, making the games more inclusive.
 
 
 
• **Key Sports at the Commonwealth Games**

questions.question: The new criminal laws aim to replace British-era laws with a focus on:
