• These reforms emphasize modernizing the legal framework to address contemporary challenges and align with **India’s democratic ethos**.
 
• The laws aim to eliminate colonial legacies that were primarily designed to **suppress dissent** and control the population.
 
• Provisions are being introduced to ensure **speedy trials, victim-centric justice**, and a robust rights-based framework.
 
• The reforms are part of efforts to establish a justice system that reflects **India’s constitutional values** and promotes fairness, equality, and transparency.

• The Indian Penal Code (IPC), Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), and Indian Evidence Act were introduced during colonial rule, primarily to serve the interests of the British Empire.
 
• The IPC was drafted in 1860 by Lord Macaulay, reflecting a colonial mindset.
 
• These laws were criticized for being outdated and not aligned with **modern democratic principles**.
 
 
 
• **Citizen rights focus:**
 
 
• The new laws aim to strengthen **fundamental rights** enshrined in the Indian Constitution, such as the right to equality, freedom, and life.

• Promoting **fair trials** and reducing delays in the judicial system.
 
 
 
• **Victim-centric approach:**
 
 
• Provisions for enhanced rights and compensation for victims of crimes.
 
• Special focus on crimes against women, children, and marginalized groups.
 
 
 
• **Modernization of laws:**
 
 
• Incorporating provisions to address **emerging crimes**, such as cybercrimes and financial frauds.
 
• Ensuring alignment with international human rights standards and treaties.

questions.question: The 3-point line in basketball is drawn at what distance from the basket in international competitions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.75 meters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 3-point line in international basketball competitions is set at **6.75 meters** (22.15 feet) from the basket.
 
• This distance is standardized by **FIBA (International Basketball Federation)**, the governing body for basketball worldwide.
 
• The 3-point line was first introduced in international competitions in **1984**.
 
• The purpose of the 3-point line is to reward players for making long-distance shots, enhancing the strategic element of the game.
 
• In comparison, the NBA 3-point line is slightly farther, ranging from **6.7 meters (22 feet)** in the corners to **7.24 meters (23.75 feet)** at the top of the arc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIBA Rules:**

 
 
• FIBA governs basketball rules for international competitions, including the dimensions of the court and the placement of the 3-point line.
 
• The FIBA court dimensions are slightly smaller than NBA courts, with a width of 15 meters and a length of 28 meters.
 
 
 
• **3-Point Line Evolution:**
 
 
• The 3-point line was first used in the American Basketball League in the 1960s before being popularized by the ABA and later adopted by the NBA and FIBA.
 
• It has significantly influenced modern basketball strategies, emphasizing perimeter shooting.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Leagues:**
 
 
• In college basketball (NCAA), the 3-point line is set at **6.32 meters (20.75 feet)**.
 
• High school basketball in the U.S. uses a 3-point line at **6.02 meters (19.75 feet)**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Gameplay:**
 
 
• The 3-point line has transformed basketball, leading to an increase in long-range shooting attempts.
 
• Teams now design plays to create open 3-point opportunities, making sharpshooters a valuable asset.

__
 
• **Chambal River** is famous for its badland topography, which is called the **Chambal ravines**.
 
• The Chambal ravines are formed due to years of soil erosion caused by water and weathering.
 
• The river flows through a **deep gorge and rugged terrain**, contributing to the formation of these ravines before it joins the Yamuna River.
 
• Badland topography is characterized by irregular and steep slopes, often unsuitable for agriculture or habitation.
 
• The statement correctly explains the connection between Chambal’s deep gorge and the formation of its ravines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Badland Topography:**

 
 
• It refers to a type of terrain that is heavily eroded and unsuitable for agriculture due to poor soil quality.
 
• Badlands typically occur in arid or semi-arid regions where water erosion is the primary shaping force.
 
 
 
• **Chambal River:**
 
 
• It is a tributary of the Yamuna River and flows through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The river originates from the Janapav Hills in the Vindhya Range.
 
 
 
• **Chambal Ravines:**
 
 
• The Chambal ravines are a result of gully erosion, which occurs when surface water runoff carves narrow channels in the soil.
 
• This type of erosion is accelerated by deforestation, overgrazing, and poor land management practices.
 
 
 
• **Ravine Rehabilitation:**
 
 
• Efforts are being made to prevent further erosion in the Chambal ravines through afforestation and soil conservation measures.
 
• Ravine reclamation projects aim to make the land usable for agriculture and to prevent desertification.
